name: DataBard
description:
DataBard turns a messy member list, RSVP export or sponsor tracker into a report you can act on — and a cleaned copy of the file.

Paste a CSV or TSV in the window, or pick a sample. A deterministic scorer checks completeness, member identity, duplicates, stale dates and contactable rows. Then one model call reads the report for your stated purpose — reporting numbers to a sponsor, emailing the list, inviting people, handing it over, or a general cleanup — and gives a verdict for that purpose plus the order to fix the report's checks in. Run the same sheet again and the reading says what moved since your last check. A deterministic audit decides what ships: every number must come from the report, every quoted name must be a real column, nothing that looks like an email or a URL is allowed through. If the reading cannot be checked, it is not shown.

You also get a cleaned copy of the sheet — duplicate rows merged by email, addresses normalised, empty rows dropped, whitespace trimmed — with a change log that says what moved. The repair happens in the window; your rows never leave it. Only scores, column names and counts reach the model.

Results save to your own Anna storage and can be reopened or copied as text. A 'roast the sheet' tone is available when you want the verdict less gently; the roast is about the spreadsheet, never the people in it.
